text.p: Jordan on Monday welcomed an Algerian pact that might pave the way for a multi-party system and general elections next year to end nearly five years of violence, the state-run news agency Petra said.
Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti issued a statement "praising the the success of the national understanding conference" and urged everyone to extend help to Algeria.

"He praised the wisdom and patience of President Liamine Zeroual in efforts to find common points between all political sectors in the country and in providing a suitable atmosphere to boost the base for national reconciliation," Petra said.

Thirty-eight Algerian party, union and other leaders signed the deal on Sunday at the end of the disputed national conference -- boycotted by two main secular parties and from which radical Islamists were barred.
Some 50,000 people have died in the bloodshed, blamed on Moslem fundamentalists.
Jordan's Moslem fundamentalists form the largest single bloc in the 80-seat lower house of parliament. They have long enjoyed a state of relative co-existence with King Hussein.
